commit_message:
lavc: convert frame threading to the receive_frame() pattern

Reorganize the code such that the frame threading code does not call the
decoders directly, but instead calls back into the generic decoding
code. This avoids duplicating the logic that wraps the decoder
invocation and allows receive_frame()-based decoders to use frame
threading.

Further work by Timo Rothenpieler <timo@rothenpieler.org>.

files.diff:
diff --git a/libavcodec/avcodec_internal.h b/libavcodec/avcodec_internal.h
index 816f39ae76..2f0aaab93b 100644
--- a/libavcodec/avcodec_internal.h
+++ b/libavcodec/avcodec_internal.h
@@ -82,18 +82,25 @@ void ff_thread_free(struct AVCodecContext *s);
  * @param avctx The context.
  */
 void ff_thread_flush(struct AVCodecContext *avctx);
 
 /**
- * Submit a new frame to a decoding thread.
- * Returns the next available frame in picture. *got_picture_ptr
- * will be 0 if none is available.
- * The return value on success is the size of the consumed packet for
- * compatibility with FFCodec.decode. This means the decoder
- * has to consume the full packet.
+ * Submit available packets for decoding to worker threads, return a
+ * decoded frame if available. Returns AVERROR(EAGAIN) if none is available.
  *
- * Parameters are the same as FFCodec.decode.
+ * Parameters are the same as FFCodec.receive_frame.
  */
-int ff_thread_decode_frame(struct AVCodecContext *avctx, struct AVFrame *frame,
-                           int *got_picture_ptr, struct AVPacket *avpkt);
+int ff_thread_receive_frame(AVCodecContext *avctx, AVFrame *frame);
+
+/**
+ * Do the actual decoding and obtain a decoded frame from the decoder, if
+ * available. When frame threading is used, this is invoked by the worker
+ * threads, otherwise by the top layer directly.
+ */
+int ff_decode_receive_frame_internal(AVCodecContext *avctx, AVFrame *frame);
+
+/**
+ * Get a packet for decoding. This gets invoked by the worker threads.
+ */
+int ff_thread_get_packet(AVCodecContext *avctx, AVPacket *pkt);
 
 #endif // AVCODEC_AVCODEC_INTERNAL_H

diff --git a/libavcodec/internal.h b/libavcodec/internal.h
index d7b0b9f880..98ab2797ce 100644
--- a/libavcodec/internal.h
+++ b/libavcodec/internal.h
@@ -51,10 +51,17 @@ typedef struct AVCodecInternal {
      * When using frame-threaded decoding, this field is set for the first
      * worker thread (e.g. to decode extradata just once).
      */
     int is_copy;
 
+    /**
+     * This field is set to 1 when frame threading is being used and the parent
+     * AVCodecContext of this AVCodecInternal is a worker-thread context (i.e.
+     * one of those actually doing the decoding), 0 otherwise.
+     */
+    int is_frame_mt;
+
     /**
      * Audio encoders can set this flag during init to indicate that they
      * want the small last frame to be padded to a multiple of pad_samples.
      */
     int pad_samples;

findings.title: submit_packet sets prev_thread to VLC-less thread during draining, causing NULL dereference after flush
findings.message: The refactoring of submit_packet() removed the early return for no-delay codecs (`if (!avpkt->size && !(codec->capabilities & AV_CODEC_CAP_DELAY)) return 0;`). The replacement guard at lines 537-538 only skips `update_context_from_thread()` during draining for no-delay codecs, but the function still proceeds to set `fctx->prev_thread = p` at line 559, pointing it to a thread that was never initialized with VLCs (coeff_vlc). When nb_threads > 2*nb_frames, prev_thread ends up pointing to a thread that never decoded anything. On the next call to ff_thread_flush(), line 991 copies context from this VLC-less prev_thread to thread[0] via update_context_from_thread(), which calls vp3_update_thread_context() and sets coeff_vlc to NULL via av_refstruct_replace(). When decoding then restarts, unpack_dct_coeffs() at vp3.c:1301 dereferences the NULL coeff_vlc pointer, causing a SIGSEGV.
findings.suggestion: Either restore the early return in submit_packet() for no-delay codecs during draining (`if (!avpkt->size && !(codec->capabilities & AV_CODEC_CAP_DELAY)) return 0;`), or move VLC synchronization out of update_thread_context into the codec init function so VLCs are set once during initialization and not dependent on prev_thread propagation. The fix commit chose the latter approach: syncing VLCs once during init via ff_thread_sync_ref() and removing the av_refstruct_replace(&s->coeff_vlc, s1->coeff_vlc) call from vp3_update_thread_context().

ground_truth.root_cause: The submit_packet() refactoring removed the early return for no-delay codecs during draining and replaced it with an incomplete guard that only skips update_context_from_thread() but still sets prev_thread to a thread without VLCs. The VLC synchronization mechanism in vp3_update_thread_context() relied on prev_thread always containing valid VLC state, an invariant that was broken when submit_packet() started running (and updating prev_thread) during draining for no-delay codecs.
